WoW: Forever

Protection Paladin

Shield tanking that generates threat from Holy damage, not weapon damage, which puts Spell Power on a tank's gear list.

WoW: Forever · Tank · Updated November 13, 2026 · Client build 1.60.1.70938 · Null Ossuary

A guide to the live game, levels 1 to 60. Talent tiers unlock at levels 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35 and 40. The one-point gold medal talents sit at 11, 21 and 31 points spent, joined in Forever by a new one at 16 points. Dual Specialization is bought from the class trainer at 40, for 50 gold by Wowhead's report.

Mechanics are Blizzard's where Blizzard has spoken: the October 15 Paladin deep dive, the November 2 development notes and the hotfixes through November 11. Numbers are the current client's, build 1.60.1.70938. A hover tooltip can lag a hotfix: where a tooltip and the prose differ, the prose is right.

The talent builds are Icy Veins' and Wowhead's, published November 4 to 6 and replayed here against the current tree. Rotation notes marked as WoWSims' are a model of a level-60 boss fight. No raid opens until December 9, 2026, so no log shows this spec tanking one, and both sites say their defensive advice may change when they see how hard raid bosses hit.

Two kinds of caveat run through these pages and they do not mean the same thing. Something marked as ours is our own reasoning, not a source's. A client or guide-site reading is a number Blizzard has not published.

What Protection is for

Holding four enemies at once, and taunting without spending a talent point. Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 3 sec. is learned at level 10 and judging it taunts, which Blizzard confirms is baseline rather than a talent. ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. is baseline at 20 for every Paladin, and Righteous FuryRighteous FuryLevel 10 · Spell · HolyCastInstantCost30% of base ManaDuration1800 secIncreases all threat generated by 33%, and all threat generated by your Holy attacks by an additional 90%. Lasts 1800 sec. raises the threat of the Holy damage both of them deal, which is why Spell Power is a tanking stat here.

Four is the number to plan pulls around. Blizzard redesigned ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. so it deals moderate damage to the first 4 enemies to enter it and very low damage to everyone else. Its stated reason is parity: a Paladin should generate reliable threat on four targets at a time, the same as a Warrior's Thunderclap, because Blizzard wants Forever to keep Classic Era's combat feel instead of sliding into the AoE-focused play of later expansions. Pull four, grind them down, and expect nothing dependable from the ring past that. Mana is the other limit.

Area grinding is not what it was. Wowhead's levelling page, updated November 6, says the Paladin's ability to grind packs was "massively nerfed" by the Retribution AuraRetribution AuraLevel 16 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantDurationUntil cancelledCauses 5 Holy damage to any creature that strikes a party member within 30 yards. Players may only have one Aura on them per Paladin at any one time. and ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec. changes, that few places between 20 and 30 reward it, and that 30 to 60 is still unknown. It still rates the spec a strong leveller because it handles several enemies at once and heals itself.

Dungeons pay less than Classic. Dungeon quests reward 50% less extra experience beyond normal quest values. Kills inside dungeons launched at 40% of their Classic Era experience and went to 60% on November 8. Icy Veins' case for levelling as Protection is that a tank finds groups easily, not that dungeons are fast.

This does not stack with other movement speed increasing effects., then come back for the Protection tree. Both end at 35 points in Protection. If you tank dungeons from level 10, use the second order.

One correction to that order is ours. As published it takes Sacred ArbiterSacred ArbiterTalentCastInstantIncreases the damage of your Holy Strike ability by 20% and causes it to refresh all Judgement effects on the target. at level 58 with 14 points in Retribution, and the talent needs 15. Take the third point of Sanctified JudgementSanctified JudgementTalent · Rank 3 of 3CastInstantGives your Judgement ability a 100% chance to return 60% of the Mana cost of the judged seal. first, as the list above does (ours, not a source's).

Wowhead's Standard raid build, updated November 4, is the same 35 Protection talents with DeflectionDeflectionTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantIncreases your Parry chance by 5%. in place of BenedictionBenedictionTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantReduces the Mana cost of all instant cast spells and abilities by 10%.. So the two sites agree on the tree and differ on one row-1 pick. Wowhead says AnticipationAnticipationTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantIncreases your Defense Skill by 20. is the flexible talent: move points out of it as gear brings you to the Defense cap.

Why these talents, briefly:

  • RedoubtRedoubtTalent · Rank 5 of 5CastInstantDamaging melee attacks against you have a 10% chance to increase your chance to block by 30%.   • PrecisionPrecisionTalent · Rank 3 of 3CastInstantImproves your chance to hit by 3%. is +1% hit per rank on every spell and attack. Stat priority

The sources no longer put Spell Power first for a main tank. Icy Veins' level-60 list is Stamina, Defense to 440, Spell Power, Intellect, Strength. Wowhead publishes three lists and tells you to start from the balanced one: Stamina, Spell Power, Hit to 8%, Defense to 440, Armor. Its offensive list leads with Spell Power and its defensive list pushes it below Block. Both give 440 Defense as the point where a boss can no longer critically hit you.

While levelling, weapon first. Icy Veins says to take Weapon Damage, Hit and critical strike early because your swings are most of your damage, and that Spell Power starts to matter once you have Retribution AuraRetribution AuraLevel 16 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantDurationUntil cancelledCauses 5 Holy damage to any creature that strikes a party member within 30 yards. Players may only have one Aura on them per Paladin at any one time. and ConsecrationConsecrationLevel 20 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 5CastInstantCost135 ManaCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration8 secConsecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 16 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area. The first 4 enemies who enter the area will take an additional 32 damage over 8 sec.. Its levelling list then runs Stamina, Spell Power, Strength, Block, Hit, Defense, Armor.

You train it at level 10, the same level other tanks get their tanking stance, and the Legacy perk The Quick and the DeadThe Quick and the DeadTalentCastInstantIncreases movement speed while dead by 10% and your helpful spells and abilities cost no resources for 2 min after being resurrected or until you enter combat. makes it free too.

Nobody's threat is cut for you any more. Blizzard removed Salvation, so the damage dealers in your group keep all their threat, and the 33% on everything is what Righteous Fury gives you to stay ahead of them (ours, not a source's). A Retribution Paladin with a two-hander is the exception: Two-Handed Weapon SpecializationTwo-Handed Weapon SpecializationTalent · Rank 3 of 3CastInstantIncreases the Physical and Holy damage you deal by 6%, and reduces all threat you generate by 20% while a two-handed melee weapon is equipped. cuts their threat by up to 20%.

Carry a shield and prefer a fast one-hander. The client's Seal of FurySeal of FuryLevel 10 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 7CastInstantCost40 ManaDuration30 secFills you with divine fury for 30 sec, causing melee attacks to deal an additional 6 Holy damage. While a shield is equipped, each attack also grants an absorb shield equal to 50% of the Holy damage dealt. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time. Unleashing this Seal's energy inflicts 32 to 34 Holy damage to an enemy and taunts the target to attack you for 3 sec. text makes the absorb conditional on having a shield equipped. Blizzard states the seal's bonus Holy damage is a constant amount per swing, unlike Seal of RighteousnessSeal of RighteousnessLevel 1 · Spell · Holy · Rank 1 of 8CastInstantCost20 ManaDuration30 secFills the Paladin with holy spirit for 30 sec, granting each melee attack an additional 2.48 to 8.64 Holy damage. Slower weapons cause more Holy damage per swing. Only one Seal can be active on the Paladin at any one time., and says outright that this favours a fast weapon while tanking. Swings per second scale both your threat and your absorb. Take mail over leather where the stats are close.

Spell power weapons come later. Wowhead flags a trap at low levels: a weapon with a heavy spell power roll carries roughly a 25% melee damage penalty, and the spell power scaling is too low early on to pay for it. It says a spell power weapon becomes the better pick "slightly higher in the levels", sooner if you fight several enemies at a time, and gives no level.

Blizzard's closing verdict is that Paladins can be highly effective tanks, with Swift JudgementSwift JudgementTalentCastInstantRange10 yd rangeCooldown60 sec cooldownUnleash the energy of a Seal spell upon an enemy. While Righteous Fury is active, Holy Strike also reduces your damage taken by 6% for 6 sec. giving more consistent control of the battlefield. Blizzard is equally plain about the gaps: no interrupt, no way to slow enemy movement, and limited range that Holy talents extend but never to a caster's reach. The four-target ceiling is design, not tuning, so do not expect it to lift.
